program_overview.title: Trading Automation & Systems Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: The systems half of quant, done properly: build, backtest and deploy automated trading systems in Python, with broker APIs, risk controls and real production discipline.
program_overview.description:
Building a strategy is one skill; running it reliably, unattended, with real safeguards is another, and this course teaches the second one. It is an engineering course, not a money-making pitch: Python for finance, technical and fundamental analysis in code, strategy design and rigorous backtesting, then portfolio theory and risk-management systems, machine learning for trading, and the part most courses skip entirely, connecting to broker APIs, paper trading, and building live systems with monitoring, logging, compliance awareness and the safeguards that stop an automated system doing real damage. Throughout, the message is repeated and honest: markets carry real risk of loss, backtests do not predict the future, and this is education, not financial advice. A finale month builds and paper-deploys a full automated system and sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.

faqs.question: What does this trading automation course cover?
faqs.answer: The systems half of quant trading, taught as engineering: Python for finance, technical and fundamental analysis in code, strategy design and rigorous backtesting, portfolio theory and risk-management systems, machine learning for trading, then connecting to broker APIs, paper trading, and building live systems with monitoring, logging, compliance awareness and safeguards. A finale month builds and paper-deploys a full automated system and sits the final exam. It is education, not financial advice.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn trading automation properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Is this financial advice? Will I make guaranteed profits?
faqs.answer: No, and be wary of anyone who says otherwise. This is an engineering and quantitative course: it teaches you to research, build, backtest and automate trading systems, not what to buy or a way to get rich. Markets carry real risk of loss, backtest results do not guarantee future returns, and we make no profit claims of any kind. What you gain is genuine, in-demand skill; what you do with real money afterwards is your own decision and your own risk.

faqs.question: How is this different from your algorithmic trading course?
faqs.answer: This course is the systems-and-execution half: how to take a strategy and run it reliably and safely through broker APIs, with monitoring, safeguards and production discipline. The algorithmic trading course is the research half: what to trade, why, and how to backtest it honestly. Many serious learners take both; that one makes you the researcher, this one makes you the systems engineer.

faqs.question: Do I need finance or trading experience to start?
faqs.answer: No. The markets knowledge and the maths you need are taught from the ground up. This course leans slightly more toward software engineering, so comfort with programming logic helps, but everything is taught step by step from the first class.
